# Observation of proof generated by semantic batches

Issue [#721](https://github.com/underpass-ai/kmp/issues/721) reproduces a loss of
member provenance: moving an observation from the packet to each member keeps
entry coordinates and source time, but dates generated links and support
associations at ingestion. Historical reads then hide proof declared earlier.

## Contract

Each semantic member declares its fact, evidence and `connect_to` links together.
Its effective observation applies to all three:

| Member observation | Observation of its generated proof |
| --- | --- |
| Explicit timestamp | That timestamp |
| Omitted, packet timestamp present | Packet timestamp |
| Omitted, no packet timestamp | Exact kernel ingestion |
| Explicit null, including with a packet timestamp | Exact kernel ingestion |

Packet provenance remains the packet's own observation. Target entry dates do
not date a new declaration. Occurrence and validity of a fact do not become
occurrence or validity of a relation. A source learned earlier and associated
later through canonical ingest keeps independent source and support dates.

## Implementation

Before merging member plans, preserve the member's effective observation in
generated non-structural `clocks` and evidence `support_clocks`. An explicit
clock object without observation requests the existing semantic command's
`default_observation_to_ingestion` policy. Resolve that default in application
alongside entry defaults, using the same kernel ingestion instant. Never stamp
it in MCP: review can wait, and retry digests must retain the unresolved command.

Canonical commands without that policy retain packet inheritance. Within an
opted-in command, absent proof clock objects retain packet inheritance; explicit
objects receive ingestion defaults. Explicit timestamps and restored clocks
with `ingested_at` remain untouched. No endpoint inference, new writer field,
protobuf field, store migration or temporal-filter change is needed.

## Acceptance and limits

Exercise native writes and reads for packet/member equivalence, mixed member
times, null overriding the packet, inclusive/exclusive temporal boundaries,
review continuation, replay, restart and export/import. Keep the independent
late-association and restored-unknown clock tests. Compare source text and
support identity, not only counts. Normal bug checks apply; no new CI gate.

The original Linde stores and failed controls remain immutable. This fixes new
writes; it does not reconstruct lost provenance in existing stored declarations
or turn missing semantic links into complete proof. Compression stays deferred.
